transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you—what has been bothering you lately that made you decide to come in today?

I’ve just been feeling really down most of the time for a long while, like my mood is constantly low and heavy. It doesn’t seem to lift no matter what I do, and after a while I felt like I couldn’t keep going like this without getting some help.
How long have you been feeling this way continuously, and have you had similar periods of low mood in the past that got better for a while before returning?

It’s been like this pretty much nonstop for about two years now. Before that I had some rough patches here and there, but they would ease up after a while—this is the first time it’s stayed this constant without really improving.

Along with feeling down, do you often feel excessively worried, tense, or on edge about many different things most days, even when nothing specific is wrong, or is it mainly the low mood that bothers you?

It’s mainly the low mood that really gets to me day to day. I do worry about things sometimes, but it doesn’t feel like I’m constantly on edge—it's more that everything just feels bleak and heavy all the time.

Before this nearly two-year stretch of feeling low most of the time, did you ever have a period of at least two weeks when you felt clearly depressed like this and then returned to feeling mostly back to your usual self for a significant amount of time?

I don’t really remember any clear “episodes” like that before this stretch. I had times when I felt low for a week or two, but it was more up and down and I’d more or less bounce back, not this kind of long, unbroken slump.

Over these past two years, have you also noticed problems like losing interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy, major changes in your sleep or appetite, feeling slowed down or restless, low energy, strong feelings of worthlessness or guilt, trouble concentrating, or any thoughts that life isn’t worth living?

Yeah, a lot of that sounds familiar. I don’t enjoy things the way I used to and my energy is pretty low most days, and it’s harder to focus on stuff like reading or even following a show. I do sometimes get thoughts that life just doesn’t feel worth much like this, but I haven’t made any plans to hurt myself.

Over these two years, have there been any stretches of at least a couple of weeks when your mood clearly improved and you felt mostly like yourself again, or has it stayed more or less the same low level the whole time without any real relief?
It’s stayed more or less at the same low level the whole time. I might have the odd day that feels a bit lighter, but never a couple of weeks where I’d say I felt like myself again.
During this long period of low mood, have you generally felt bad about yourself or like you’re a failure, or felt quite pessimistic that things will ever really get better for you?
Yeah, I pretty much feel like that all the time now. I often think I’ve messed up my life and that nothing I do is really going to change anything, so I don’t expect things to get better.

Over these two years, have your symptoms been so severe that they significantly interfered with your ability to work, study, or manage daily responsibilities, or have you generally been able to keep functioning, even if everything feels like a struggle?

I’ve mostly been able to keep going with work and basic responsibilities, but everything takes more effort and I’m slower and more forgetful than I used to be. I make more mistakes, have trouble focusing in meetings or on tasks, and often put things off because my head feels foggy and I can’t decide what to do first.

Have you ever had periods lasting several days when your mood was unusually high or irritable, you needed much less sleep, had a lot more energy than usual, or felt so driven or confident that others thought you were acting unlike your usual self?
I don’t think I’ve ever had anything like that. I can’t remember a time when I needed less sleep or had a big burst of energy or confidence—if anything, it’s usually the opposite.

Thinking about these last two years, have there been any months when you went more than two weeks without feeling clearly depressed or low most days, or has the low mood been present nearly every day throughout this entire period?
The low mood has been there pretty much every day throughout this whole period. I can’t think of any stretch longer than a few days where I didn’t feel clearly down most of the time.

Therefore F32.10 is removed and the current candidate list is [F34.1]. Further questioning about other medical/psychiatric comorbidities and functional impact could still be useful, so the assessment is not yet final.

opening_question.question: Hello, it’s good to meet you—what has been bothering you lately that made you decide to come in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports a nearly continuous depressed mood for about two years, with no periods longer than a few days without low mood, along with low energy, anhedonia, poor concentration, pessimism, and low self-worth. Functioning is impaired but preserved (able to work, though slower, more mistakes, and procrastination). There is no history of distinct major depressive episodes before this chronic course, and no evidence of manic or hypomanic episodes. The chronicity (≥2 years), near-daily low mood, and subthreshold but persistent depressive symptoms without full syndromal major depression for most of the time are most consistent with dysthymia/persistent depressive disorder (F34.1). Major depressive episode (F32.1) and mixed anxiety and depressive disorder (F41.2) were considered but are less likely given the long-standing, unremitting course and lack of prominent anxiety.
